source_quote: For n>=2 let q_n(i)=n/(2 H_{n-1} i(n-i)), 1<=i<n, where H_m=sum_{j=1}^m 1/j. Conditional on a split i,n-i assume independent daughter trees of their respective sizes. If S is external path length and C is the sum of the absolute differences of daughter leaf counts, then G_n(u,v)=E[u^S v^C] satisfies G_1=1 and G_n=sum_i q_n(i) u^n v^{abs(n-2i)} G_i G_{n-i}. This identifies each finite-n joint law; it does not identify a limiting law.

Put d^A_n(i)=t^A_n(i)+mu^A_i+mu^A_{n-i}-mu^A_n. For two finite-second-moment additive indices A,B, their covariance K_n=sum_i q_n(i)(K_i+K_{n-i}+d^A_n(i)d^B_n(i)). Setting B=A gives the variance recursion. Initial one-leaf values are deterministic.

source_quote: Let (B^k)_{k in Z} be mutually independent standard Brownian drivers, and let the entire sequence of positive finite lengths (L_k) be independent of every driver, with partial sums diverging in both directions. Concatenate B^k restricted to [0,L_k] and pin the join between -1 and 0 at time and value zero. The resulting process has two-sided Wiener law at that origin. The lengths may have any joint law; no iid, uniform bound or finite-mean assumption is needed. Path-dependent Brownian stopping lengths are not covered.

Truncating the nonnegative mixture to b_k<=M omits exactly epsilon_{k,M}=(1/M!) sum_{lambda partition of M, lambda_1<k}(f^lambda)^2, where f^lambda is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape lambda. The density L1 error is epsilon_{k,M}; all event-probability errors and the total variation after normalization are at most epsilon_{k,M}, using sup-event total variation. For k=2 epsilon=1/M!.

source_quote: Under the stationary RSK rank mixture for drift dX_i/dt=X_i and rate-one Poisson space-time left jumps, the first-row label pair is (1,b) with weight (b-1)/b!, b>=2. For 0<x_1<x_2, put g=x_2-x_1. Its joint density is exp(-x_2) F(g), where F(g)=sum_{r>=0}(r+1)g^r/(r!(r+2)!). Consequently X_1~Exp(1) is independent of X_2-X_1, whose density is exp(-g)F(g); F(0)=1/2. The marginal tail is P(X_2>x)=exp(-x) sum_{r>=0}x^r/(r!)^2.

source_quote: In nearest-neighbor Z^2, for L=8^j join squares [-L,L-1]^2 and [3L,5L-1] x [-L,L-1] by {(x,-L):L<=x<3L}. The induced sets are connected, nested and exhausting, have volume 8L^2+2L and edge boundary 20L-2, hence form a Folner exhaustion. Any internal path between their squares uses all 2L+1 corridor edges. In iid bond percolation with p<1, its probability is at most p^(2L+1). This does not disprove existence of a different good Folner sequence.

source_quote: For a closed K subset of R^2, call a boundary point z accessible from a component U of R^2 minus K if a continuous path starts at z and lies in U at every positive parameter. Join two complement components in a graph when some point of K is accessible from both. Two distinct points outside K can be joined by an arc meeting K finitely many times exactly when their components are joined by a finite graph path. Thus the simultaneous all-pairs property is equivalent to connectivity of this countable graph. Closure contact alone is insufficient.
